summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a right thigh abscess and hematoma, confirmed by CT imaging, and underwent incision and drainage. Cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus, and she was treated with vancomycin initially, then transitioned to oral levofloxacin. Her kidney function, which was acutely impaired with creatinine rising to 3.7, improved to 2.9, attributed to prerenal causes from infection and volume status. Tacrolimus was increased to 5 mg twice daily to maintain immunosuppression. She received one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia. Wound care included twice-daily wet-to-dry dressing changes with pain managed using acetaminophen and dilaudid. She was discharged home with home health services, on a five-day course of levofloxacin, with follow-up arranged with primary care and transplant surgery.
problems: Cutaneous abscess of right lower limb
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus infection as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
